summary: This bill amends the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965 to bar federal funds from any public school that lets employees or contractors give students under 18 counseling, therapy, or guidance on gender identity or help them hide such information from parents, and lets parents sue schools for violations.

scores.thoughts: The bill conditions receipt of existing federal education funds on compliance with new restrictions but does not authorize new spending, cut overall appropriations, or change aggregate spending levels. It is a regulatory condition rather than a spending measure.
The bill contains no provisions related to taxes, tax rates, deductions, or revenue collection.
While the bill restricts school-based counseling on gender identity, it does not address healthcare systems, insurance coverage, public vs. private delivery, or medical regulation.
No provisions address firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
No provisions relate to immigration, borders, visas, or immigrant protections.
No provisions address abortion access or restrictions.
No provisions address military or defense spending or policy.
No provisions address environmental regulations or climate policy.
No provisions address welfare programs, food assistance, or other safety-net benefits.

The bill amends the Elementary and Secondary Education Act to impose content-based restrictions on public schools as a condition of receiving federal funds. It engages education policy but does not alter funding levels, expand federal programmatic involvement, promote school choice, or advance privatization; the core focus is a social-issue prohibition rather than structural education reform.
No provisions address drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled substances.
No provisions address sentencing, policing, or criminal-justice reform.
No provisions address trade, tariffs, or globalization.
No provisions address deficits, debt reduction, or fiscal targets.

The bill explicitly prohibits public schools from providing any counseling, therapy, guidance, or social-transition support related to gender identity for students under 18 and bars schools from helping students withhold such information from parents. It directly limits institutional support and affirmation of transgender or gender-nonconforming identities in federally funded schools, constituting a clear restriction on policies that expand LGBTQ+ accommodations.
No provisions address foreign aid or international assistance.
No provisions address voting access, election procedures, or voter ID.
No provisions address technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight.
No provisions address unions, collective bargaining, or worker/employer relations.
The bill centers on parental notification and restrictions on gender-identity counseling rather than religious exemptions or conflicts between civil-rights protections and religious liberty.
